transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. What brings you in to see me today?

Well, I'm here because I just haven't been myself lately. Ever since my choir friend passed away—it was real sudden—I just... I don't know, I'm having a hard time. 

I find myself crying over little things, like the potluck lists. And I get all worked up about phone calls that I used to handle real easy. I've even started missing some of the church planning things, and I never, ever would have missed those before. I just need some help figuring out how to get back on track.
How long have you been feeling this way since your friend passed away?
It's been about a month now. Yeah, right around a month since she passed away, and this has just been going on ever since then.
Do you find yourself enjoying things you used to like before your friend passed away?
I... I'm not really sure. I haven't really thought about it like that. To be honest, I just haven't been doing much of anything lately to even notice if I still enjoy it or not.
Are there things that you used to enjoy doing before your friend passed away that you've tried to do since then?

No, not really. I just... I haven't even tried. I usually do a bit of baking or tend to my garden, but I just haven't had the drive to go out and do any of it lately. I've mostly just been staying around the house, so I haven't really tested it out to see if I'd still enjoy those things right now.
Do you often find yourself thinking about your friend who passed away?

I'm not really sure. I mean, of course she crosses my mind, but... I wouldn't say I'm constantly thinking about her. I haven't really noticed myself just sitting around dwelling on specific memories or anything, if that's what you mean. I mostly just... I don't know, I just haven't been doing much of anything.
Do you feel like you've lost interest in things that used to bring you pleasure?

I don't know if I'd say I've lost interest, exactly. It's more like... I just don't have the urge to do them right now. Like I was saying, I haven't even tried to bake or get out in the yard. So it's hard to tell if they would still bring me pleasure or not, because I just haven't had the energy to even start.
Do you feel sad most of the day?

No, I wouldn't really say that. I mean, I'm not sitting around crying or feeling down all day. It's not so much sadness, I guess. I just... I mostly just feel like I don't have the energy to do much of anything.
Have you lost any weight since your friend passed away?
No, I don't think so. I haven't actually stepped on a scale recently, but... my clothes still fit the same as they always do. So, no, I haven't noticed any changes with my weight.
Do you feel guilty about anything related to your friend's death?
No, not really. I mean, it was a heart attack, so it was very sudden. There wasn't anything anyone could have done. So... no, I don't feel guilty about it. Just tired.
Do you feel hopeless about the future?

No, I wouldn't say hopeless. I know life goes on, and... well, I know things will eventually be okay. It's just hard to find the energy for it right now. But no, I don't feel like there's no hope or anything like that.
Do you find yourself preoccupied with memories of your friend?

No, I wouldn't say preoccupied. I mean, I think about her, naturally... but I'm not dwelling on it all the time. It's not like I just sit around thinking about the past all day. Memories just pop up every now and then, but that's about it.
Do you think you would enjoy baking or gardening if you were to start doing them again?

I don't really know. I haven't tried doing either of those things lately. I suppose I might enjoy them a little if I actually got started? But honestly, right now, just the thought of getting all the baking supplies out or working in the dirt just feels like a lot of work. I'm just too tired to even try, so it's hard to say if I would actually enjoy it.
Do you think you would still find joy in the things you used to do if you had the energy to do them?

I'm really not sure. It's... it's hard to separate the two, I guess. Maybe I would? I suppose if I actually had the energy and wasn't so drained, I might like doing them again. But since I feel the way I do right now, it's just difficult to even picture it. So, I honestly don't know for sure.
Do you think you would still want to participate in choir if you had the energy for it?

I... I don't really know about choir either. I guess it's like the baking and gardening. It's just hard to imagine wanting to go and be around all those people and sing when I feel this exhausted. Maybe if I felt like myself again, I'd want to go back, but right now, I just can't say for sure.
Do you think there are activities you used to enjoy that you now have no interest in at all?

I don't think so. I mean, I can't really think of anything where the interest is just completely gone. It's more like what I was saying before... it's the lack of energy. I don't feel like I've permanently lost interest in the things I used to like. I just don't have the drive to actually do them right now.
Do you find that your feelings and reactions since your friend passed away are mostly related to the loss itself, rather than to other areas of your life?

I'm not really sure. I mean... losing her is definitely the biggest thing on my mind, but it's hard to say if my feelings are strictly just about the loss itself. It kind of feels like everything is just mixed together right now. I haven't really thought about trying to separate it out like that, to see what's causing what, so I can't say for certain.
Do you think your feelings and reactions are mostly about missing your friend and wishing she was still here?

I mean, I definitely miss her terribly, and I do wish she was still here. But I don't know if I can say it's mostly about that. It's just... everything feels heavy right now. I haven't really broken it down in my head to figure out exactly what part of this is just missing her and what part is... well, everything else.
Do you often have intense yearning or longing for your friend who passed away?

I don't think I'd use those words. I mean, I miss her, obviously. But I don't really have that... intense yearning you're talking about. It's not like I'm sitting around constantly pining for her all day. It's more just that general heavy feeling I mentioned, rather than a sharp longing like that.
Do you wish you could have done something to prevent your friend's death?

No, not really. I mean, it was a sudden heart attack, so there wasn't anything anyone could have done. I know that in my head. I don't sit around wishing I could have stopped it or feeling guilty about it, because I know it was just... one of those things that happens.
Do you think your life will ever return to being as fulfilling as it was before your friend passed away?

I haven't really thought about it like that. I mean... I suppose I think things will get back to normal eventually. I don't feel like my life is over or that I'll never be happy again, if that's what you mean. It's just a bit of a struggle right now. But I do think it will get better in time.
